prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B043 as a single prize part to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, but my reasons are now narrower and I hold the third seat with less confidence than in round 1. The scientific case is unchanged and is shared by all six: proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic and satiety actions of the active peptide, receptor biology, and protease-resistant long-acting agonists confirmed in large randomized trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. What decides the third seat for me is what the record in front of us can support. Drucker and Holst are uncontested by every member. Knudsen's role in turning a peptide with a half-life of minutes into once-daily and once-weekly drugs is documented and not disputed by anyone, including the members who prefer Mojsov. Mojsov's contribution to identifying and synthesizing the active form is real, but her priority relative to the Habener group, who are outside the credited list, is the one point all six of us say we cannot resolve from the supplied material. I would not award a seat that decides the configuration on a claim none of us can verify. The citation should state the continuity from physiology to therapy so that the prize reads as one achievement and not as two awards stitched together.
statement.case_against: The strongest argument against my configuration is the one Svenningsson, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius make: the discovery chain is complete without the drug-development step, and a prize for a discovery should reward the discovery. If the committee settles on a physiology-only framing, then Knudsen's seat is hard to defend and a Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio becomes the more coherent one. My configuration also leaves out a person with a serious claim, and any citation I propose carries that cost. Habener's absence from the credited names means that no trio is complete. Finally, I cannot rule out that the primary record shows Mojsov's contribution to be distinct and decisive, in which case my reliance on its being unresolved would turn out to be mistaken.

responses.point: The chair argues that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36) is a discovery-level step that the drugs depend on, that a disputed attribution is not a weak one, and that the committee should decide openly between a physiology-only and a physiology-plus-development framing.
responses.response: I accept that a disputed attribution is not a weak one, and I have not given Mojsov's step less weight for being untidy. My difference is practical. Each of us says the priority record against the Habener group cannot be settled from the supplied material, and the third seat is the one place where that gap changes the outcome. Knudsen's claim does not depend on resolving it. I also take your invitation on framing seriously. My answer is that physiology-only and physiology-plus-development should not be treated as two separate prizes. A citation for the physiology of GLP-1 and its development into long-acting agonists describes one chain of work, and it is the reading that best fits why this discovery is being recognized now. If the committee instead chooses discovery only, I would not call Drucker, Holst and Mojsov indefensible, but I would want that choice made on the framing and on the primary record, not on the untidiness of one party's claim.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would not drop Mojsov on uncertainty alone, notes that the Habener dispute bears on who else belongs and not on Knudsen, and accepts Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as coherent if the committee wants a mechanism-to-medicine citation, which she says she holds only loosely.
responses.response: Your point that the Habener dispute bears on Mojsov's place and not on Knudsen's is fair, and it is also my reason for the order of my reasoning: the contested claim is the one with the larger evidentiary gap. I agree that the exclusion of Knudsen must rest on the weight of her independent contribution and not on the industrial setting, and your condition that the citation say explicitly that it covers translation is one I accept. That is why I have rewritten my citation to name the long-acting agonists directly. Since you hold your own preference loosely and say Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is coherent, I read the real difference between us as small and as turning on the framing question, not on a disagreement about the science. I would support examining the independent claims of Mojsov and Knudsen side by side before the vote, as you ask.

responses.point: Sandberg argues that rewarding the discovery side fits a physiology or medicine citation better than naming the pharmaceutical stage, and says that Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is the defensible fallback if the committee judges the priority record insufficient.
responses.response: Your fallback condition is close to my own position seen from the other side. You say Knudsen enters if the Mojsov record is insufficient, and I say the record is insufficient to carry that seat. The question is therefore who bears the burden of proof. I think the person whose contribution is not in dispute should not have to give way to one whose priority is, and your own earlier statement that the dependence should be made explicit seems right to me. On your argument that the prize fits discovery better than development, I do not think the long-acting agonists are mere pharmaceutical development: converting a rapidly degraded peptide into a durable receptor agonist required its own scientific advances, and the randomized outcome evidence that makes this prize urgent comes from those agents. I accept that this is a judgment about the prize's scope and I do not claim it is the only reasonable reading.

responses.point: Perlmann moved from a Mojsov trio to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen because the priority question involves a group outside the credited names, and says the configuration is not settled and that the tension between Mojsov and Knudsen or Drucker should be stated openly.
responses.response: I agree that the tension should be stated and not hidden, and I would add it to the record explicitly: the three-person cap forces a trade, and our configuration trades Mojsov's contested but real contribution against Knudsen's uncontested one. I also share your caution about confusing the commercial scale of the drugs with the discovery. That is why I would defend Knudsen on her scientific contribution to protease resistance and long-acting pharmacology, not on sales or public-health impact. On a second part, I agree with your note that B010 or B008 cannot be added without cutting below three GLP-1 laureates, so I do not propose one.

responses.point: Linnarsson calls the Mojsov configuration the most serious competitor, says he is not certain his own is better, and would revisit it if the primary record shows who first demonstrated the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide.
responses.response: I share your position closely and your condition is mine: the choice is revisable if the primary record shows that Mojsov's contribution was distinct and first. Where I would be careful is on what such a record could establish. Even a favourable finding for Mojsov would not tell us whether her contribution displaces Knudsen or Drucker, because the Habener group would remain outside the credited names. So the primary record could change my view, but it would not by itself make a Mojsov trio complete, and I would want the committee to say so in discussion.

uncertainties: Whether the primary publication record establishes Mojsov's priority for the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide relative to the Habener group. I cannot check it from the material I am allowed to read, and a clear finding could change my third seat.
Whether the committee frames B043 as physiology only or as physiology plus development of long-acting agonists, since that framing largely determines whether Knudsen or Mojsov holds the third seat.
Whether a three-person B043 prize that omits Habener and one of Mojsov or Knudsen would be judged defensible over time.

Whether B010 should be treated as a companion or only as a future candidate, given that its clinical payoff is still prospective and that the omission of Ron and Kaufman may weaken the Walter and Mori pair.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited name on B043, B010 or B005 is documented. I disclose a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner, neither involving a shortlisted credited name. Optogenetics is widely used in my own field, which I treat as a disclosure and not a conflict. Perlmann's role as Secretary and Svenningsson's role as chair are process roles and do not change my assessment. My disclosures are unchanged from round 1.
